title: News: comment on the news and follow a talk show

blocks.text: Egyptians talk about current affairs everywhere: at coffee, in taxi, in the family, on social media. And in the TV talk shows, which are among the most followed programs in the Arab world, the conductor opens in fuṣḥā, the guest responds in Egyptian, and the conversation passes from one to the other also in the same sentence. In this unity you learn to speak of a news in Egyptian (what happened, what you think, what people say), to recognize the Egyptian caught up in debates, with the words of the fuṣḥā pronounced to the Egyptian (saqāfa, istismār, qānūn), to take and defend the word in a discussion and to distinguish a news from a voice (išāʿa) when it circulates on social media. Nine weeks, in parallel with B2-03, B2-04 and B2-05.

rows: 12–13 9 weeks (weeks) 166–174), about 1,5 hours per week in two blocks

blocks.text: Materials This unit, a tutor or an Egyptian partner, extracts of talk shows or current Egyptian programs (Appendix C)
Targets. At the end of the unit you know:
1. report and comment on news in Egyptian, distinguishing facts, opinions and voices;
2. recognizing the words of fuṣḥā in the Egyptian pronunciation read ( ⁧ث⁩ → s, ⁧ذ⁩ → z, ⁧ق⁩ → q in translated words);
3. follow a short extract of talk show where fuṣḥā and Egyptians alternate;
4. take the floor, politely interrupt and defend its position in a debate;
5. ask and verify the source of news circulating on social media.
Nine-week plan (two blocks from 40–45 minutes per week).
